# alber.me

> Personal website of Alexander and Franziska Alber, researchers based in Germany. Besides profile pages it hosts a collection of free interactive browser tools (React, client-side only): every tool runs entirely in the browser, nothing is uploaded, no accounts, no tracking.

Most tools are bilingual English/German (switch with `?lang=en` / `?lang=de`); the parenting tools are German-first. Content is licensed CC BY-NC 4.0.

The projects listed under "Separate projects on the same domain" are independent: not part of this site and not tools in its collection, each with its own subject, repository and appearance. They appear under alber.me only because GitHub Pages applies this account's custom domain to its project pages as well, so each repository is served from a path on this origin.

## People

- [Alexander Alber](https://alber.me/alexander/): Diagnostic engineer at Hitachi Energy (power transformer and tap changer diagnostics), previously DLR; publications, patents, CV. Also published as Alexander Pollok.
- [Franziska Alber](https://alber.me/franziska/): PhD candidate in theoretical computer science, University of Regensburg; automata over infinite alphabets, formal verification.

## Tools

- [E-Book Converter](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/ebook-converter.html): Converts EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, Markdown, HTML and plain text to EPUB, MOBI, Markdown, HTML, a self-contained HTML reader, LaTeX, DOCX, a Pandoc bundle or plain text; all parsing and writing happens in the page, so the book is never uploaded, and DRM-protected files are detected and refused. Before converting, a book can be edited: a table of contents rebuilt from the headings or edited by hand, a typographic cover drawn from title and author or cut from an image, search and replace on the text without touching the markup, and typographic quotes, ellipses and dashes for German or English. A repair pass fixes MOBI files whose cover points at a path that leads nowhere. Whole batches convert to one zip with the same clean-up applied to every file, several books merge into one omnibus with a chapter group each, and the images can be pulled out of a book.
- [Terrain Erosion Simulator](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/erosion-simulator.html): Simulate hydraulic erosion on a grayscale heightmap with live 3D before/after preview and 16 bit PNG export.
- [Trophy Sculptor](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/trophy-generator.html): Designs award sculptures that print upright without support material: no surface leans past the overhang limit you set, and a layer-by-layer check on the finished solid confirms it. The height is the one number to set; every other length scales with it. Eleven families: a lattice cage, a flame of turning ribbons, a twisted stele, quartz crystals in a half-sunk asteroid, bismuth hopper crystals stood on their corners, a tree whose branching follows Murray's law, a three-phase power transformer, a classic cup, a slit cone, a flying wing (B-2, kite or F-22) and a graph (the lasso of a model checker's counterexample, or the Hasse diagram of a three-element set's subsets as a cube on its corner). The plinth takes an engraving in a single-stroke font, cut as by a V-bit whose flanks also stay within the limit. Export as one STL, or as plinth and sculpture in two colours that print apart and join by a boss and socket that need no support either. Models go straight on to Print Nest for a transport case.
- [Heightmap to STL](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/heightmap-to-stl.html): Turn a grayscale heightmap into watertight STL terrain tiles for 3D printing.
- [Print Nest](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/print-nest.html): Builds a fitted transport case for a 3D print from its STL: a two-part capsule, a cover block or a draped shell, the first two printable without support. Takes models straight from the Trophy Sculptor.
- [Image Editor](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/image-editor.html): Non-destructive photo editing (crop, scale, rotate, draw, text, perspective warp) with a reorderable history stack.
- [Painting Simulator](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/painting-simulator.html): Paint with pigments instead of pixels; colors mix by two-constant Kubelka-Munk optics (blue and yellow make green), pressure comes from cursor speed, the brush runs out of paint, paper has tooth, wet paint smears, and every realism layer has its own off switch.
- [Pixel Forensics](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/pixel-forensics.html): Maps over a photograph that show what the eye does not: the JPEG block grid and its origin, the quantisation table inverted to an exact IJG quality and cross-checked against the pixels, sensor noise, resampling traces and a line profile, each with its limits stated. Draws no conclusions itself.
- [Colormap Designer](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/colormap-designer.html): Builds a colormap for the constrained case the published maps do not cover: colours partly given, a background that is not negotiable, or a quantity that is an angle. Give it colours and it returns a dozen finished candidates per run for sequential, diverging or cyclic, each optimised in OKLab onto those colours and reparametrised by arc length so equal steps in the data are equal perceptual steps. Next to the chosen one stands the damage report: the lightness profile, the local perceptual rate, a dichromat simulation, the contrast against your own background, and the five energy terms separately rather than only their sum. The lightness is read back out of the emitted 8-bit values rather than off the ideal curve, and the count of candidates says when the colours genuinely do not allow a dozen different ones instead of padding the list with near duplicates.
- [Color Extractor](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/color-extractor.html): Find which colours an image is made of: palettes of two to nine colours by k-means in OKLab, each colour's share, the image redrawn in any palette, and export as hex codes, CSS variables or JSON.
- [Color Grading](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/color-grading.html): Grade a photo in the browser: colour wheels, curves, HSL secondaries, split toning, a live histogram, waveform and vectorscope, palette matching from the Color Extractor and a Sony ARW raw intake. Exports PNG, JPEG or a .cube LUT.
- [Background Remover](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/background-remover.html): Remove a white, near-white or single-colored background from a photo or scan entirely in the browser: flood fill from the edges leaves enclosed white areas intact, correction for unevenly lit scans, soft edges without a white fringe, PNG export with transparency.
- [Patch Similarity Explorer](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/patch-similarity.html): Upload an image, click any spot, and see a heatmap of how similar every other region is, from DINOv3 vision transformer patch features computed entirely in the browser. A second view colors the features by PCA and segments them with k-means.
- [Pixel to Vector](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/pixel2vector.html): Convert a PNG, JPEG or WebP into a clean SVG entirely in the browser: black-and-white tracing with subpixel accuracy on anti-aliased edges, or a color mode that quantizes to a small OKLab palette and stacks one layer per color so no seams show. One slider from exact to simple, per-layer control.
- [Book Recommender](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/book-recommender.html): Fantasy and science fiction recommendations from about 2,500 books and series, with probabilities that are calibrated rather than decorative. A 32-factor matrix factorisation trained offline folds your ratings in by ridge regression, live in the browser, and returns expected stars with a predictive interval and the probability that you would rate a book 4 stars or higher; on held-out readers the 90% intervals cover 90.4% and every probability decile lands within two points of reality. Onboarding asks about the books you probably know and that shrink the uncertainty most, each recommendation names the ratings it comes from, and a series card shows how readership and reception hold up volume by volume. Also a 2-D taste map, a leave-one-out check of the model against your own ratings, and CSV import and export.
- [LLM Detector](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/llm-detector.html): Calibrated probability that an English or German text was written by a language model, with typical AI phrases highlighted and open methodology.
- [Language Zipper](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/language-zipper.html): Identify a language by compression - an order-3 byte model with Witten-Bell interpolation trained on 87 natural languages (Tatoeba) and 28 programming languages, plus a UPGMA family tree and an MDS map built from the same cross-entropy measurements.
- [Token & Character Counter](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/token-counter.html): Count tokens (o200k_base and cl100k_base tokenizers), characters, words, sentences, lines and bytes live.
- [Local LLM Frontier](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/local-llm-frontier.html): Which open-weight language model fits your GPU, and how good it is. Set VRAM, context length and KV cache precision: the chart places every model at every quantization by the memory its weights and KV cache actually need (the cache computed per attention type, so sliding-window layers are not overcharged), against a shared intelligence index drawn as a band rather than a point, and names the closed frontier model of roughly the same quality. Mixture-of-experts models are marked, and with a memory bandwidth entered the tool estimates decode speed, which is memory-bound. The model data is a dated snapshot.
- [Claude Code settings.json Generator](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/claude-code-settings.html): Click together a Claude Code settings.json (permission rules, Read and Edit path rules with resolved anchors, model, environment variables).
- [System Prompt Builder](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/system-prompt-builder.html): Click together a personal system prompt for your chatbot - one variant per aspect (tone, pushback, expertise, code, ambiguity handling and more), every block editable, output in English or German.
- [Text Corruptor](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/text-corruptor.html): Zalgo text with a gradient: a spline sets how corrupted the text gets from start to end, applied clause by clause with fourteen Unicode effects. Plus the classic Unicode text conversions.
- [Quap Lab](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/bayes-rethinking.html): Fits Bayesian models in the browser on your own CSV or JSON, written as a formula list the way one writes them on paper: ~ for stochastic and <- for deterministic relations, twelve distributions and ten functions. Fits by quadratic approximation at the posterior mode, with a grid cross-check that reports where that approximation breaks down, or by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with NUTS, reporting Rhat, bulk and tail effective sample sizes and divergences. Generalised linear models need no special support: wrap the linear part in inv_logit or exp and give the outcome the distribution it actually has. Indexed parameters give one intercept per group, and a shared prior on those makes a multilevel model, which the sampler handles in non-centred coordinates, because there the posterior is a funnel and a Gaussian at the mode has the wrong shape. Posterior summaries with compatibility intervals, prior and posterior predictive simulation, and several models side by side compared by WAIC and PSIS-LOO with Pareto k diagnostics; comparisons across different outcomes or row counts are refused. A fitted model downloads as a Python file that predicts at new inputs with nothing beyond numpy and pandas. Not supported: correlated varying effects and mixtures. Notation, approach and examples follow Richard McElreath's Statistical Rethinking; this is an independent implementation.
- [Lambda Diagrams](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/lambda-diagram.html): Type a term of the untyped lambda calculus and see it drawn as a Tromp diagram. Normal-order beta reduction then runs step by step, each step animated as a smooth morph from one diagram to the next, until the term reaches normal form or a limit of 8000 steps. A result that is a known term (identity, a combinator, successor, addition, multiplication, predecessor and others) is named. Church numerals, booleans and the S, K, I and Y combinators are built in as examples. German and English.
- [Ruler Title Finder](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/title-finder.html): A deadpan consultation for the newly enthroned. Seven questions score 44 historical ruler titles (emperor, caliph, shogun, tsar, doge and more) by a transparent additive score in points, with no probabilities anywhere, and recommend the best fit. Each title comes with real history: etymology, notable holders, occupational statistics and how the title ended.
- [Leverage & Ruin](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/leverage-ruin.html): How much leverage is too much? Monte Carlo simulation of a leveraged ETF over long horizons: volatility drag, the Kelly optimum, break-even leverage and wipe-out probability, plus uncertainty about the expected return, fat-tailed innovations and a Merton jump diffusion mode in which one crash day ends a leveraged position outright. The ensemble average rises with leverage while the typical path peaks and turns back down.
- [German Marginal Tax Wedge](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/tax-wedge.html): How much of the next euro a German employee keeps, as a curve over the whole income range, stacked by levy: income tax, solidarity surcharge, church tax, social insurance, employer shares and benefit withdrawal, under 2026 law. German and English.
- [Reaction Diffusion](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/reaction-diffusion.html): A Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion system full screen on the GPU, steered by dragging a cursor across a map of the known pattern regimes (solitons, worms, mazes, mitosis); seeds can be painted with the pointer.
- [Sun over Regensburg](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/regensburg-sun.html): Does the sun still reach a given spot in Regensburg at a given minute. Clicking the map answers for that exact point by marching a ray across the official Bavarian surface model at one metre resolution, buildings and trees included, combined with a terrain horizon profile from a 40 km ring; a time slider recomputes the shadow of the whole visible area, and the picked spot also reports its hours of sun for the day. Solar position by the NOAA method with refraction and daylight saving. German and English.
- [Ripple Tank](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/ripple-tank.html): A 2D wave equation live on the GPU, full screen: plane or point sources, slits, lenses, prisms and freehand walls, showing reflection, diffraction and refraction.
- [Input Shaping Calculator](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/input-shaper.html): ZV, MZV, ZVD, ZVDD, EI and multi-hump EI shapers on a damped spring-mass system, with Klipper configuration output.
- [Race Time Predictor](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/laufzeiten-rechner.html): Predict race times for 1 km to 50 km from personal bests, Riegel formula with personally fitted exponent.
- [Choir Part Trainer](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/choir-part-trainer.html): Practise one part of a choral score from MusicXML, MXL or MIDI: per-voice mix, slower tempo, transposition, loops over bars, scrolling notation and live pitch feedback from the microphone.
- [Sheet to MIDI](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/sheet-to-midi.html): Upload a PDF of cleanly engraved choir music, get practice MIDI back. Optical music recognition entirely in the browser, per-voice playback (solo, all, or one voice loud and the rest quiet), suspect measures flagged for proofreading, MusicXML export for MuseScore.
- [Sing Trainer](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/sing-trainer.html): Practise hitting notes with live microphone pitch detection; scales, triads and generated melodies per voice range.
- [Vowel Map](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/vowel-map.html): Live formant tracking from the microphone; LPC estimates F1 and F2, the voice moves as a point through the vowel chart, with calibration on your own corner vowels, snapshots and a target vowel for choir vowel blending.
- [Drug Concentration Visualiser](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/medikamenten-spiegel.html): Plots the blood level of a drug over the day and the days after. Drag intake times on the chart, combine doses with immediate- and extended-release forms, and watch accumulation build toward steady state. A linear one-compartment model, so intakes simply add up; extended-release forms follow a Weibull release profile rather than the plain Bateman curve, and bupropion's active metabolite gets a curve of its own, formed in the blood and already during the first pass through the liver. 19 substances are built in, from caffeine and ibuprofen to methylphenidate, lisdexamfetamine, levodopa, sertraline and lithium. German and English.
- [A Model of Psychohistory](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/psychohistory.html): Posterior predictive futures of a galactic civilization; Bayesian ensemble simulation as an interactive art piece.
- [Grabby Aliens Simulator](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/grabby-aliens.html): Interactive 3D simulation of the Hanson grabby aliens model: expanding civilizations fill a periodic box and suppress later origins, with statistics on human earliness, first contact times, and a light-delayed sky view.
- [Flow Field Defense](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/flow-field-defense.html): Maze tower defense in which the pathfinding is visible: the cost-to-go field, threat coverage and enemy occupancy are drawn under the board, and a tower is a cell with a traversal cost rather than a wall.
- [Cobra 6DOF](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/spaceship-6dof.html): A six-degree-of-freedom spacecraft flown with a 3Dconnexion SpaceNavigator over WebHID, which makes it Chromium-only and pointless without the hardware. The hull is an honest rigid body rather than a kinematic toy: its inertia tensor is integrated over the actual mesh by tetrahedral decomposition and diagonalized onto principal axes, Euler's equations run in the body frame so the intermediate axis is genuinely unstable, and wall contacts are resolved with accumulated sequential impulses, so a grazed corner imparts torque and leaves the ship tumbling. Rendering is wireframe with backface hidden-line removal in the manner of Elite 1984, inside a box gridded on all six walls because free flight has no floor. Thrust, torque, hull geometry, cap deadzone and curve, per-function axis assignment and a second-order Butterworth camera tracker on SO(3) are all adjustable, with the resulting traverse and turnaround times reported in seconds rather than in newtons.
- [Asteroid Corridor](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/asteroid-corridor.html): A six-degree-of-freedom sandbox among turning asteroids, flown with a 3Dconnexion SpaceNavigator over WebHID (Chromium only), with the rigid-body physics of Cobra 6DOF and contact against the drawn rock geometry.
- [Subway Sauce Guide](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/subway-sauces.html): Heatmap rating every Subway sauce against every sandwich on a scale from -3 to +3, for the German and US menus of several months, with the sauces sortable by name or by average. German and English.
- [When to Close the Windows](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/optimal-venting.html): When to shut the windows on a hot day and when to reopen them, from nothing but the day's minimum and maximum temperature: a thermal simulation of one room over every pair of closing and reopening times, with the optimum marked against the usual rule of thumb. German and English.
- [Meal-Prep-Planer](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/meal-prep-planer.html): German-language batch-cooking planner that turns a week of planned meals into one Sunday cooking timeline, a merged shopping list and a printable note per dish.
- [QR Code Generator](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/qr-code-generator.html): QR codes encoded in the page, so nothing is uploaded and no redirect service sits between the code and its destination. Free colours with transparency, PNG and SVG export, presets for WiFi, vCard, email, SMS, geo coordinates and phone numbers. The error-correction level is explained rather than merely offered: an anatomy view colours every module by data, redundancy or fixed pattern and by interleaving block, and an occlusion control counts damaged codewords against the real per-block budget, reporting the largest centred square a logo could cover. Eight module shapes, from plain squares to one that joins only the modules that happen to spell a Korean letter, each with its measured cost in resolution. One of them is genuinely animated: small snakes crawl along the dark modules and every frame stays the same valid symbol, exported as a looping GIF or a CSS-animated SVG.
- [PCB Art Designer](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/pcb-designer.html): Design decorative light-up PCB art and export what a fab needs, entirely in the browser. It works like a colouring book: trace a reference image into dividing contours or draw them with lines, rectangles, circles and strokes, then click each area to say what it is made of: bare FR4, soldermask over FR4, exposed gold-plated copper, soldermask over copper, silkscreen, or a cutout milled out of the board. Bare FR4 on both sides makes a translucent light window, and the tool keeps the copper clear behind every window for you. LEDs, a CR2032 holder and a button go on the back, with the nets derived from the parts rather than drawn in a schematic; a check reports whether every net is one piece of copper and whether trace widths, clearances, annular rings and drills are manufacturable. A 3D view with day and night lighting shows the LEDs through the windows. Exports Gerber and Excellon files to the KiCad 9 conventions that Aisler and JLCPCB expect, or an editable KiCad project.
- [Self-Guided Walking Tour](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/walking-tour.html): Offline walking tours in the browser: a map drawn from OpenStreetMap, a route over the actual footpaths and one commentary per stop, written to be read standing in front of it. Two tours, the Buda Castle District in Budapest and the Regensburg old town, fifteen stops each.

## Parenting tools (German-first)

- [Baby-Basics](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/baby-basics.html): Distribution curves for sleep, feeding and crying in a baby's first year, with percentile bands.
- [Pregnancy Timeline](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/pregnancy-timeline.html): When common pregnancy symptoms typically start, peak and fade.
- [Child Development Timeline](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/child-dev-timeline.html): Milestones from 0 to 48 months plus WHO growth curves.
- [Due Date Distribution](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/geburtstermin-verteilung.html): Probability distribution of the actual birth date around the estimated due date.
- [Name Finder](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/namenfinder.html): German baby name finder for the stage where every good name either belongs to a colleague or sits at number 3. Filters by origin (Germanic, Hebrew, Nordic, Romance and more), syllable count, length, final sound and how a name sounds, soft or striking. Each name comes with its meaning, spelling variants, its current rank in the German top 500 and its curve by decade, so rising names and names that peaked in the eighties are visible. German, with an English version.
- [Birth Decisions Explorer](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/geburtsentscheidungen.html): Decisions around giving birth with quantified effects and evidence grading.
- [Parental Leave Planner for Germany (Elterngeld)](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/elterngeld-planer.html): Plans Elterngeld, the German statutory parental allowance under the BEEG, together with income tax and the split of months between both parents. Computes Basiselterngeld and ElterngeldPlus for both, including the partnership bonus, and includes the progression clause: Elterngeld is tax-free but raises the tax rate on the rest of the year's income, which a plan that ignores it pays for in the tax return. Instead of one optimal plan it shows a Pareto front of all splits where more time at home necessarily costs more, and the chosen split can be adjusted by hand afterwards. Computed under 2026 law; only useful for a child born in Germany. German, with an English version.
- [Daycare Infections](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tools/kita-infekte.html): How many daycare infections per year are normal, with percentile bands.

## Separate projects on the same domain

- [transformer-twin-lab](https://alber.me/transformer-twin-lab/): Interactive browser demos on digital twins of power transformers, in the context of CIGRE JWG A2/D2.65: Duval triangle and pentagon under measurement uncertainty, a thermal mini-twin after IEC 60076-7, a moisture twin for paper and oil, and the five capability levels of a digital twin on one shared model.
- [transformer-twin-lab llms.txt](https://alber.me/transformer-twin-lab/llms.txt): That project's own llms.txt, describing it in full.
- [infinite alphabets](https://alber.me/infinite-alphabets/): Interactive playground for parametrized automata and variable automata over infinite alphabets, companion to two papers by Franziska Alber and Philipp Rümmer (CIAA, ATVA): simulation, products and checks, plus an animation of the ATVA proof idea.
- [infinite alphabets llms.txt](https://alber.me/infinite-alphabets/llms.txt): That project's own llms.txt, describing it in full.

## Optional

- [Tools overview](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/): Landing page listing all tools with descriptions.
- [Tool map](https://alber.me/miscellaneous/tool-map.html): A node-link map of how the tools connect: data handoffs through browser storage, shared engines, plain links.
- [Cats](https://alber.me/cats/): Pictures of three cats. Loki, Mango and Kimchi.
- [Design conventions](https://alber.me/design-conventions.html): How the tools on this site are built: the no-build single-file stack (Pico CSS, React, htm), the three-skin colour ladder, the shared components, the htm traps and the equivalence checker that caught them.
- [Privacy](https://alber.me/datenschutz.html): Privacy notes (German).
